h1: San Elizario, Clint, Anthony & Vinton Court Ticket Lawyer — El Paso, TX
intro: El Paso County's smallest towns each run their own municipal court, with clerk offices that close early and, in several cases, close on Fridays. That makes a missed date costly and an attorney's appearance unusually useful. Robert Navar handles all four for a flat $69.
summaryHeading: A small-town court is still a real court, and its office hours are short
summary: San Elizario Municipal Court is at 12004 Socorro Rd., Suite B, phone 915-302-2050, open Monday through Thursday 7:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Clint Municipal Court is at 125 Brown St., phone (915) 851-1600, open Monday through Thursday 8 to 5 and Friday mornings only.

Anthony Municipal Court is listed by the Texas Office of Court Administration at P.O. Box 1269, Anthony, TX 79821, phone (915) 886-3272; Anthony Town Hall is at 401 Wildcat Drive. The Village of Vinton lists its office at 436 E. Vinton Rd., (915) 886-5104.
The ticket is in one of these courts only if that town's police department wrote it. Sheriff, DPS and constable citations on the same roads go to the El Paso County JP precinct noted on the ticket.
Our flat fee in any of these courts is $69 per citation; extra tickets from the same stop are discounted add-ons. Hire online or call 915-503-1600.

sections.heading: First, Confirm the Ticket Is Actually in a Town Court
paragraphs: Each of these towns has its own police department and its own municipal court, and each court hears only the citations written inside that town by its own officers. Clint's court page describes the job plainly: it "processes fine-only Class C Misdemeanors within our jurisdiction including Town Ordinance violations." The agency line on your citation is the test. If it names the town's police department, the case is in that town's court.

The confusion comes from the county offices next door. El Paso County's Justice of the Peace Precinct 6-1 sits at 190 N. San Elizario Rd. in Clint, and Precinct 7 at 435 E. Vinton Rd. in Vinton, a few doors from the Village office. Those are county courts, and they take the Sheriff's, DPS and constable citations written on the same roads; the county's instruction is that a citation from any agency other than the El Paso Police Department goes to the JP precinct noted on the ticket. Not sure? Use our free ticket and warrant lookup before you drive anywhere.

sections.heading: San Elizario Municipal Court
paragraphs: San Elizario is the Lower Valley town just past Socorro, and its police write tickets on Socorro Rd, Alameda Ave (Highway 20) and the roads between them. The city lists its Municipal Court at 12004 Socorro Rd., Suite B, San Elizario, TX 79849 (mail to P.O. Box 1458), phone 915-302-2050, open Monday through Thursday, 7:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The page names a court coordinator and a deputy court clerk, and says payment plans or alternatives can be discussed by phone.

The city accepts payments in person, by mail, by phone and online through a third-party vendor that adds a convenience fee, and its page describes periodic warrant amnesty windows during which warrant fees are removed for a person who contacts the court and pays in full; it warns that partial payments do not clear a warrant. Before paying anything, remember that paying a Class C citation enters a plea and results in a conviction. We ask every San Elizario client for a current insurance card and registration first, because a paperwork ticket presented with proof of compliance is the one most likely to be dismissed outright.

sections.heading: Clint Municipal Court
paragraphs: Clint sits east of Socorro along Alameda Ave and FM 1110, with I-10 just north of town; many drivers ticketed there live in Horizon City or far-east El Paso and are passing through. The Town of Clint lists its Municipal Court at 125 Brown St., Clint, TX 79836, phone (915) 851-1600, office hours Monday through Thursday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., and Friday 8:00 a.m. to noon. The page names the municipal judge and the court clerk and says citations can be paid at that office.

For school-zone speeding and other charges where a driving safety course is unlikely to be granted, we ask for deferred disposition or a reduction to a non-moving charge. When we file an appearance in Clint we calendar the next setting ourselves and handle any continuance within the flat fee.

sections.heading: Anthony Municipal Court
paragraphs: Anthony, Texas is at the northwest corner of the county on the New Mexico line, where I-10 and Doniphan Dr cross into Anthony, New Mexico, so out-of-town drivers and commercial drivers are a large share of the court's traffic cases. The Texas Office of Court Administration's directory lists Anthony Municipal Court at P.O. Box 1269, Anthony, TX 79821, phone (915) 886-3272. El Paso County lists Anthony Town Hall at 401 Wildcat Drive, phone (915) 886-3944, and the town's website as anthonytx.org. We could not open the town's own court page, so confirm hours by phone before visiting.

Commercial drivers need a different plan. Texas law does not allow a court to use deferred disposition or a driving safety course for a CDL holder's traffic offense, so an Anthony case for a trucker turns on the citation's defects and on negotiating a charge that does not count as a serious violation under the commercial rules. Tell us at intake if you hold a CDL. The county's JP Precinct 7 in Vinton takes trooper and deputy tickets from the same stretch of I-10.

sections.heading: Vinton Municipal Court
paragraphs: Vinton is the small Upper Valley village between Canutillo and Anthony along Doniphan Dr and Vinton Rd, with I-10 along its edge. El Paso County lists the Village of Vinton's office at 436 E. Vinton Rd., Vinton, TX, phone (915) 886-5104. The Village's municipal court did not appear in the Texas Office of Court Administration directory we checked, so we are not publishing a separate court address or docket schedule for it; call the Village at the number above to confirm where a Vinton citation is docketed, or let our office do it.

Whatever the schedule, the handling is the same. We file the appearance, request a recall of any warrant that has issued (see traffic warrant recall), and ask the court to set the ticket on its next docket, where it is negotiated for dismissal, deferred disposition or a course dismissal, each in the court's discretion.

sections.heading: What $69 Covers, and What to Send Us
paragraphs: We charge $69 per citation in the San Elizario, Clint, Anthony and Vinton courts. The fee covers the appearance, every docket setting and the closing paperwork; court fees for a deferral or course are set by the court. Extra citations from the same stop are $10 to $30 add-ons at checkout, and warrants are $35 for the first plus $20 for each additional one. A paid ticket is a conviction, and a traffic conviction may affect insurance premiums depending on the driver's history, carrier and other rating factors. Our goal is to pursue the best available outcome based on the citation, driving record, court and circumstances.

Do not pay the ticket, do not request defensive driving yourself, and do not wait for a docket date that may be weeks out. Send the citation through the online form or call 915-503-1600. The consultation is free; se habla español.

faqs.q: Which court has my ticket if I was stopped in Clint or San Elizario?
faqs.a: If that town's police officer wrote it, the town's municipal court: Clint's at 125 Brown St., San Elizario's at 12004 Socorro Rd., Suite B. If a Sheriff's deputy, DPS trooper or constable wrote it, the El Paso County JP precinct noted on the ticket (the county's Precinct 6-1 office is at 190 N. San Elizario Rd. in Clint). Our free lookup form can confirm it.

faqs.q: What are the office hours of these courts?
faqs.a: San Elizario posts Monday through Thursday, 7:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Clint posts Monday through Thursday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., and Friday 8:00 a.m. to noon. We could not confirm Anthony's or Vinton's hours on an official page; call (915) 886-3272 for Anthony Municipal Court and (915) 886-5104 for the Village of Vinton.

faqs.q: What is the attorney fee for Anthony or Vinton tickets?
faqs.a: A flat $69 per citation in any of the four courts. Additional citations from the same stop are $10 to $30 add-ons; warrant recalls are $35 for the first and $20 for each additional one.

faqs.q: Do I have to drive out to the court?
faqs.a: Generally not. We appear for you on the docket day and negotiate with the prosecutor. A personal appearance is needed only if the case is set for trial.

faqs.q: I got the ticket passing through on I-10 and I live out of state. Can you still help?
faqs.a: Yes. Out-of-state drivers are a large share of Anthony and Vinton cases. We handle the case by phone and email, and you do not have to return unless the case were set for trial.

faqs.q: I missed my court date in one of these towns months ago. What now?
faqs.a: There may be a warrant and a hold on your license renewal. Call us the same day. We file the appearance, request the recall and get the ticket onto the next docket; see traffic warrant recall.
